obligations.description: The complete NV_NVDLA_csb_master root has84 native ports and no top parameters. Falcon-side request acceptance and final response outputs use rising nvdla_falcon_clk and asynchronous active-low nvdla_falcon_rstn. Request dispatch,client response capture and response ingress use rising nvdla_core_clk and asynchronous active-low nvdla_core_rstn. The clocks are independent and may pause; timing is determined by their actual edge history,including coincident edges using pre-edge state. There are14 clients in this numeric order:cfgrom,glb,mcif,cdma,csc,cmac_a,cmac_b,cacc,sdp_rdma,sdp,pdp_rdma,pdp,cdp_rdma,cdp. Request RAM has4 records of50 bits; response RAM has2 records of34 bits. Both channels have one additional input staging record. The fixed functional build uses FPGA,NO_PLI,PRAND_OFF,real low-phase-latched clock enables and no power-clock bypass. No random FIFO-stall or FIFO-depth override is applied. pwrbus_ram_pd has no functional effect in this build. The independent model uses the same84 ports with no formal parameters or external macro requirement.

obligations.description: Apply the following rule independently to each FIFO channel at its writer clock,with depth D=4 for requests or D=2 for responses. Track a pending input bit P,internal full/busy bit B,interface blocked bit H,occupancy C modulo2D,a modulo-D write position,and a retained input staging record. Before an edge,commit=P AND NOT B; returned is one recovered reader event from R003. Compute nextC=(C+commit-returned) modulo2D and nextB=(NOT returned) AND (nextC==D). Writer ready is NOT H. An offered record replaces input staging exactly on offer AND NOT H. A commit writes the PRE-edge staging record at the current write position,advances that position modulo D and sends one event. H next is nextB when offer1; when offer0 it is P AND nextB AND NOT commit. P next is offer AND NOT H unless PRE-edge P AND B,in which case P holds. C and B become nextC and nextB. Thus a full RAM can retain one additional accepted record in staging:an empty channel with no reader progress accepts5 request records or3 response records before blocking. When the RAM becomes full on an idle offer0 edge,ready need not fall. A blocked offer is not accepted; it does not overwrite staging. Request ready exposes the request channel H only; there is no external response ready.

obligations.description: Each channel sends committed write-event counts and reader-event counts modulo2D. A sent count advances only for its event,including during long idle gaps; it does not advance merely because its clock runs. Writer-to-reader visibility passes through three receiving-clock samples. At a reader edge,if the previously settled third sample differs from the local processed write-event count,the reader processes exactly one event:advance that local count by1 modulo2D,read the current RAM position into a retained output record,advance the read position modulo D,send one reader event,and set the channel delivery-valid register1. Otherwise delivery-valid becomes0 and the output record holds. Reader readiness is permanently1; there is no client backpressure into this eager read. In the reverse direction the three writer-clock samples of reader events advance only when (C+commit) modulo2D is nonzero; otherwise those samples hold. A previously settled third reverse sample unequal to the locally processed reader-event count recovers one returned event at that writer edge and advances the local processed count by1. Receiving stages sample PRE-edge values; an update to the third stage on an edge is acted upon on a later edge. No single fixed absolute transfer latency applies across arbitrary clock phases,pauses and event backlog. After request-channel delivery,dispatch uses the prior delivery-valid/data at the next core edge; final Falcon response classification similarly uses prior response-channel delivery-valid/data at its next Falcon edge.

obligations.description: Pack an accepted Falcon request as50 bits {nposted,write,wdat[31:0],addr[15:0]}. addr is a16-bit word address. Decode its6-bit page addr[15:10],equivalent to the byte address {addr,2 zero bits} masked at bits17:12. Pages0 through13 select the corresponding numeric client from R001; every page14 through63 selects the dummy client. All1024 low-bit offsets within each page have the same client selection. There are no active bdma,rbk or cvif destinations. Each client63-bit request payload is {7 zero bits,nposted,write,wdat[31:0],6 zero bits,addr[15:0]}; the entire original16-bit address is retained. The shared50-bit dispatch record captures channel data whenever prior request delivery-valid1,even during reset because this particular register has no reset. Client payload registers capture that shared PRE-edge dispatch record according to R005; there is a distinct data-capture phase after decode.

obligations.description: Each client has a decode-pending bit Q,an externally visible request-valid bit V,and a retained50-bit payload. On a core edge outside reset,set Q next1 if prior request delivery-valid selects this client; otherwise set Q next0 if current client ready1 OR PRE-edge V0,and otherwise hold Q. V next1 if PRE-edge Q1; otherwise V next0 if current ready1,and otherwise hold V. Capture the shared PRE-edge dispatch record into this client payload when PRE-edge Q AND (current ready OR NOT PRE-edge V). Thus an isolated dispatched request first sets Q,then one core edge later sets V and its payload. A blocked V holds its last captured payload until the stated capture condition occurs. New deliveries are consumed eagerly and may replace or coalesce pending client state; client readiness does not stop either FIFO reader. Repeated traffic and arrivals while a client is stalled obey these equations,without an assumption that every accepted Falcon request eventually becomes a distinct client handshake. V0 does not clear its payload; every client payload remains continuously visible,including invalid cycles.

obligations.description: At every core edge outside reset,each client response-valid register becomes its current native response-valid input. Its34-bit payload register captures the native response payload only when that input valid1; otherwise its payload holds. The offered merged response on a later core edge has valid equal to the OR of all14 registered client valids and the registered dummy response-valid. Its34-bit data is the bitwise OR of every valid registered response payload,including the dummy payload; invalid payloads contribute zero. Multiple simultaneous clients are admitted in this fixed build and are merged by bitwise OR,not priority or serialization. This offered response enters the finite response FIFO under R002. The input clients and dummy are not backpressured by response-FIFO readiness:offers while that FIFO interface blocked are discarded and are not retried. One valid held for several core edges creates repeated offers. Response payload bit33 selects read/write class,bit32 is error and bits31:0 data; the error bit is carried through the FIFO but does not otherwise change final outputs.

R-p8-csbm-001.description: Run independently scheduled core and Falcon clocks and initialize their active-low resets; exercise requests and responses through native ports.
Pause and resume each clock while the other runs, and include offset/coincident receiving edges.
Exercise all14 client interfaces and power-input changes in the fixed complete native build, without clock/power bypass or FIFO-depth override.

R-p8-csbm-002.description: Stop request-reader progress, offer more than four requests and include the fifth accepted staging record plus later blocked offers.
Stop response-reader progress, offer more than two responses and include the third staging acceptance plus later dropped offers.
Exercise idle at full, removal of offers, reader credit recovery, repeated fill/drain and pointer/event wrap for both channels.

R-p8-csbm-003.description: Send isolated requests and replies under independent clocks and compare delivery/classification at their actual receiving-edge histories.
Use bursts and separately paused clocks so forward synchronization, backlog processing and delayed credit recovery are observable.
Include coincident edges, event-count wrap and empty occupancy gaps before new traffic, exposing pre-edge third-sample processing and occupancy-gated reverse synchronization.
